applicability: All dispositions apply to systemd 257 [Timer] units on a Linux laptop (system manager), AccuracySec/RandomizedDelaySec at defaults unless stated. No service logs or hardware timing data were supplied; operational behavior beyond manual statements is marked as inference or missing evidence.

1: P1 Persistent= (last-trigger stored; immediate trigger if >=1 missed elapse)

2: P1 Persistent= (only has an effect on OnCalendar= timers)
P1 Options (monotonic timers independent of wall-clock)
P1 Options (past-activation immediate elapse only OnBootSec/OnStartupSec)
P1 WakeSystem= (suspend CLOCK_BOOTTIME only, not power-off)
3: P1 Description (already-active unit not restarted; no new instances)
P1 Description (RemainAfterExit=yes unsuitable for repetitive timers)
4: P1 Options/OnCalendar (do not necessarily expire at precise time)
5: P1 Options table (OnUnitInactiveSec relative to last deactivation of activated unit)

P1 OnCalendar (time-sync.target ordering; RTC warning; single activation after sleep)

conditions_exceptions: Persistent catch-up requires >=1 missed elapse, timer enabled/active at boot, timestamp file on disk; fires once per activation. OnUnitInactiveSec never elapses if target never deactivates; first post-boot elapse depends on recorded deactivation and service Type. AccuracySec window plus TimerSlackNSec/load bound start precision. Calendar scheduling requires correct realtime clock. No evidence was supplied for service Type/RemainAfterExit, Unit= identity, boot times, or clock-sync state.
